about: Industrial Handling (IHA), FH Technikum Wien master's programme, winter term 2021, after the lecture notes of Berger (2021), chapters 1–6, and the Übungsskript and solved Übungen 5_1, 5_2 and 5_3 (Berger 2021a). Pages are the PDF pages of each chapter's file, read in their text layer on 2 Nov 2026; Blatt numbers where the footer was readable. The printed solutions are used where they exist (chapter 3, p. 113; chapter 6, p. 19; the Übungen 5_1–5_3); the rest were worked by hand from the course's equations and say so. tests/unit/labs-data.test.js recomputes every answer with the core and fails if they disagree.
examsAbout: The tasks of the past exams in Prüfungen\ (Prüfung 15, 16, 18, and 17 inside Prüfung 18), by year; Old\MMR17 holds byte-identical copies (SHA-256). The exams are photos or scans of graded students' sheets; only 2015 has a Musterlösung. Most tasks are constructions on a scale drawing: those a lab works are asked here with the exam's given values; those no lab draws (Kutzbach plans, three-position synthesis) are listed with a note. Each task's questions also appear in its lab's Practise tab.

labs.title: How many drives? The mobility count
labs.idea: Count the links and joints of a plane mechanism and the count says how many drives it needs: one freedom, one drive, and it moves as driven; none, and it is a structure.

equations.note: Plane and spherical mechanisms (b = 3): n links with the frame, g1 joints with one freedom, g2 with two
Constrained motion (Zwanglauf); F = 0 a determinate structure, F < 0 an indeterminate one

practice.question: The cam mechanism of chapter 3 has n = 5 links, g1 = 4 and g2 = 2. How many drives does it need?
A Watt six-bar has 6 links (frame included) and 7 hinges. What is F?
practice.source: Worked by hand from ch. 4, p. 23

labs.title: Which link turns? Grashof's rule
labs.idea: If the shortest and longest links together are shorter than the other two, some link can turn fully; which mechanism you get depends on where the shortest link sits.

equations.eq: lmin + lmax < l′ + l″ rotating; = change point; > rocking
equations.note: Four-hinge chain (4D): umlaufend, durchschlagend, nicht umlaufend
Slider-crank chain with offset e, crank and coupler the two links

practice.question: Frame 100 mm, crank 30 mm, coupler 90 mm, rocker 70 mm. By how many mm is lmin + lmax shorter than l′ + l″?
practice.source: Worked by hand from ch. 4, p. 26
practice.solution: 30 + 100 = 130 against 70 + 90 = 160: 30 mm shorter, so the chain rotates; the shortest link is the crank beside the frame, a crank-rocker.

practice.question: A slider-crank has crank 30 mm and coupler 100 mm. Up to which offset e does the crank still turn fully?
practice.source: Worked by hand from ch. 3, p. 81

labs.lecture: Berger (2021), chapter 4, and chapter 3 for the slider-crank chain

labs.title: The transmission angle
labs.idea: The coupler pushes the rocker well only when it meets it near a right angle; the smallest such angle over a turn tells you whether the mechanism runs smoothly.
labs.law: μ = acute angle between coupler and rocker at B, μ ≤ 90°

equations.eq: μ ≤ 90°, the acute angle between absolute and relative path tangents at B
equations.note: Definition; the least values lie where crank and frame are folded or stretched

equations.eq: cos γ = (l² + c² − AB0²)/(2lc), μ = min(γ, 180° − γ)
equations.note: The cosine rule in triangle A B B0, worked from the definition; the course draws it

labs.title: Instant centres and the speed ratio
labs.idea: Every two links of a mechanism turn, for a moment, about a common pole; the pole of crank and rocker tells you how fast the rocker turns for a turn of the crank.

equations.note: The number of poles of n links
P13 has the same speed as a point of crank and of rocker; worked from the pole's definition

practice.question: How many poles has a six-link mechanism?
practice.source: Worked by hand from ch. 4, p. 47

labs.title: Dead-centre synthesis of the crank-rocker
labs.idea: Say where the rocker should stop at each end of its swing, and the crank and coupler follow, because at the dead centres crank and coupler lie in one line.

equations.eq: φ0, ψ0 measured in the same sense from the inner to the outer dead centre
equations.note: The course's construction: angles φ0/2 and ψ0/2 at A0B0 give the pole P, circles ka, kb carry Aa, Ba
From the stretched and folded positions
At constant crank speed

practice.question: Kap. 4 Aufgabe 5 asks for φ0 = 160°. What is the ratio of working to return time at constant crank speed?
practice.source: Worked by hand; data from the Übungsskript, Kap. 4 Aufgabe 5
practice.solution: 160/(360 − 160) = 160/200 = 0.8: the working stroke is the quicker one.

labs.title: Two-position synthesis: the pole P12
labs.idea: Any move of a body in the plane from one position to another is one turn about a single point, the pole, found where the perpendicular bisectors of two of its points meet.

equations.eq: P12 where the bisectors of A1A2 and B1B2 meet; φ12 halved by them
equations.note: The turn φ12 about P12 is directed

practice.question: A bar moves from A1(30; 0), B1(60; 0) to A2(−30; 0), B2(−30; 30). What is the y coordinate of the pole P12 in mm?
practice.source: Worked by hand; data from the Übungsskript, Kap. 4 Aufgabe 1
practice.solution: The bisector of A1A2 is x = 0. B1B2 has its middle at (15; 15) and runs along (−90; 30); its bisector −90x + 30y = −900 meets x = 0 at y = −30.

practice.question: By how many degrees does the bar turn about P12?
practice.source: Worked by hand; data from the Übungsskript, Kap. 4 Aufgabe 1
practice.solution: A1 − P12 = (30; 30) at 45°, A2 − P12 = (−30; 30) at 135°: a quarter turn, counter-clockwise.

labs.title: Coupler curves and their cognates
labs.idea: A point on the coupler draws a curve, and two more four-bars draw exactly the same curve: if one linkage sits badly, a cognate may fit.
labs.law: Roberts–Chebyshev: three four-bars, one coupler curve
labs.lawTex: F_0 = A_0 + k\,(B_0 - A_0), \quad k = \frac{C - A}{B - A}

equations.eq: Every coupler curve of A0ABB0 is also drawn by A0A′F′F0 and B0B′FF0
equations.note: Roberts–Chebyshev theorem
The third pivot: A0B0F0 similar to ABC; k a complex ratio

labs.title: Motion laws and their characteristic values
labs.idea: A normalised law f(z) says how the output moves over its stroke; four numbers taken from it, Cv, Ca, Cj and CM, scale its peak speed, acceleration, jerk and torque.

equations.note: Normalised law, rising

equations.tex: \dot y = y'\dot x, \quad \ddot y = y''\dot x^2 + y'\ddot x
equations.note: From the drive angle to time

equations.eq: Cv = max|f′|, Ca = max|f″|, Cj = max|f‴|, CM = max|f′f″|
equations.note: Characteristic values
Peak acceleration over the drive angle

equations.eq: f = a1z + a2z² + a3z³ + a4z⁴ + a5z⁵
equations.note: 5th-order polynomial from boundary values; a1 = f′(0), a2 = f″(0)/2
7th power
